title: Receiver tools: notch, blanker, NR, attenuator
idea: Each receiver control fixes one kind of trouble. Notch for a carrier, blanker for pulses, noise reduction for hiss, attenuator for overload, reverse sideband for a CW neighbour, and dual VFOs for split operation.

rows: Noise blanker: cuts gain during each pulse
Dual VFO: transmit on one, listen on the other

compare.how: Removes a carrier in the passband.
Drops gain during each noise pulse.

traps.wrong: To eliminate receiver interference from impulse noise sources
traps.why: Impulse noise is the noise blanker's job. The notch removes carriers.
It reduces receiver gain during each pulse.

traps.wrong: To reduce excessive audio level on strong signals
traps.why: It protects the receiver from overload, not your ears.

traps.wrong: To permit full duplex operation -- that is, transmitting and receiving at the same time
traps.why: Dual VFO is for split: transmit on one frequency and listen on another, not at the same time.
